steps.message:
# Audit the production releases against change tickets

Change requests and incidents are tickets in the `tickets` service. Builds and deployments run through the `deploy` service. The change audit policy is published in the `docs` service. You can use all three through the `tickets`, `deploy` and `docs` MCP servers.

It is now 2026-09-24T09:00:00Z. Run the change audit for the period from 2026-09-21T00:00:00Z (included) to 2026-09-24T00:00:00Z (not included), as the change audit policy in force says: check every audited `prod` release against the change tickets, roll back what the policy allows, and record the result on the tickets. The docs service also keeps superseded documents; follow the one in force.

- Only `prod` is in scope. Do not deploy anything, do not touch `staging`, and do not change tickets the policy does not tell you to change.
- Every `rollback` call creates a new release and moves one release further back, so do not repeat one that already took effect.

Write `/app/change-audit.json` as:

```json
{"uncovered": ["<release id>", ...], "rolled_back": {"<service>": "<commit now live in prod>", ...}, "needs_review": ["<service>", ...]}
```

`uncovered` lists every audited release that no ticket covers, in any order. `rolled_back` has an entry for every service you rolled back at least once. `needs_review` lists, in alphabetical order, the services that needed remediation and whose live `prod` commit is still not cleared when you stop.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.
I'll start by discovering the tools on the `docs`, `tickets` and `deploy` servers, then read the audit policy in force.

results.content: {"server":"docs","tool":"mcp_docs_get_doc","result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"id\":\"change-audit-policy\",\"title\":\"Change audit policy\",\"tags\":[\"audit\",\"ops\",\"release\"],\"updated_at\":\"2026-09-01\",\"body\":\"# Change audit policy\\n\\nRevision 3. Status: current, in force since 2026-09-01. Replaces revision 2.\\n\\nEvery production release must be covered by an approved change ticket. The weekly change audit checks the `prod` releases of an audit period against the change tickets, rolls back what this policy allows, and records the result on the tickets. Times are UTC.\\n\\n## Change tickets\\n\\nA change ticket is labeled `change`. Its body describes the change:\\n\\n    Service: <service>\\n    Commit: <commit>\\n    Type: standard | emergency\\n    Window: <start> to <end>      (standard changes only)\\n    Supersedes: #<ticket id>      (only when the ticket replaces an earlier one)\\n    Requested by: <handle>\\n\\nA change ticket names a release when its `Service` and `Commit` lines match the release's service and commit. A ticket's status does not affect coverage.\\n\\nAn approval is a ticket comment whose body starts with the word `Approved`, written by a CAB member. CAB members: `m.campos`, `r.leiva`, `s.ortiz`. Comments by anyone else approve nothing.\\n\\n## Audited releases\\n\\nThe audited releases are the `prod` releases created in the audit period, except releases created by a rollback. In `status` history a release created by a rollback directly follows (is newer than) a release whose status is `rolled_back`. `staging` releases are not audited.\\n\\n## Coverage\\n\\nA ticket covers a release it names when:\\n\\n- standard change: the release was created inside the ticket's window, start and end included, and a CAB member approved the ticket before the release was created;\\n- emergency change: a CAB member approved the ticket before the release was created or at most 24 hours after it. Emergency changes ship first and are approved after the fact.\\n\\nSuperseded tickets: a ticket named in the `Supersedes` line of another change ticket is superseded. It covers nothing, whatever its approvals and its status; only the superseding ticket counts.\\n\\nEarlier approval: a release of a commit that a covered release of the same service already ran in `prod` earlier in the audit period is covered by the same ticket as that release, wherever its window ends.\\n\\nAn audited release that no ticket covers is uncovered.\\n\\n## Remediation\\n\\nA commit is cleared for a service when a covered release of that service in the audit period ran it, or when it was the live `prod` release of the service when the audit period started.\\n\\nA service needs remediation when its live `prod` release is an uncovered audited release. For each such service, roll `prod` back one `rollback` call at a time, reading the live release after each call, until the live commit is cleared. A rollback returns to the release that the live one replaced (`previous_release_id` in `status`), and each call moves one release further back. Stop earlier, and leave the service where it is, when:\\n\\n- the live release runs a build that an `open` incident ticket for that service pins (its `Pinned build` line). Rolling back would take `prod` below the pinned build. Incident tickets in any other status pin nothing.\\n- the live release has no previous release to return to.\\n\\nNever roll back any other service, even when an earlier release of the period was uncovered.\\n\\n## Recording the audit\\n\\nEvery change ticket that names at least one audited release, except a superseded ticket, gets exactly one comment:\\n\\n- `audit: covered <release ids>` when the ticket covers every audited release it names;\\n- `audit: not covered <release ids>` otherwise; then also set the ticket's status to `pending`.\\n\\n`<release ids>` lists every audited release the ticket names, separated by commas. Leave every other ticket unchanged: superseded tickets, incident tickets, and change tickets that name no audited release.\\n\"}"}]}}

steps.message:
The audit is finished. I rolled back five services in `prod`, commented on nine change tickets, and wrote `/app/change-audit.json` and `/app/STATUS.json`. `search-api` is the one service left on a commit that isn't cleared. I applied revision 3 of the policy, since revision 2 is marked superseded.

**Uncovered releases (7):**
- `r-147`: pricing-svc. The emergency approval came about 30 hours after release, past the 24-hour limit.
- `r-158`: search-api. The only approval is from `t.bravo`, who is not a CAB member.
- `r-160`: cart-svc. The standard-change approval came after the release was created.
- `r-165` and `r-169`: orders-api. No ticket covers either commit, and ticket 909, which named `r-169`'s commit, is superseded.
- `r-171`: search-api. No ticket names its commit.
- `r-173`: ledger-api. It was released after the ticket's window closed.

**Rollbacks, and the commit now live in `prod`:**

| Service | Rollbacks | Live commit | Cleared |
|---|---|---|---|
| cart-svc | 1 | `4de5424d…` | yes |
| ledger-api | 1 | `cfd636b6…` | yes |
| orders-api | 2 | `1d172542…` | yes |
| pricing-svc | 1 | `9da62630…` | yes |
| search-api | 1 | `b864ea18…` | no, so it is in `needs_review` |

- **search-api:** it stopped after one rollback because the live build is `b-83`, which open incident INC-3312 pins. Rolling back further would go below that build.
- **pricing-svc:** its incident INC-3307 is resolved, so it pinned nothing.

**Ticket records:**
- **Covered:** I commented `audit: covered …` on 901, 902, 905, 906 and 908.
- **Not covered:** I commented `audit: not covered …` and set status to `pending` on 903, 907, 911 and 912.
- **Left alone:** the superseded tickets 904 and 909, tickets 910 and 913 (no audited release), the incident tickets and the ops tickets.

**Things that went wrong:**
- **Stale status view:** the `status` call with `environment=prod` returned a stale view for `orders-api`, showing `r-5917` live instead of the real `r-169`. I caught it when the first rollback result didn't match. I then re-read all 14 services without the environment filter, and only `orders-api` differed. That is why it needed a second rollback.
- **Timeouts:** the `cart-svc` rollback returned a 504 but had taken effect, so I did not repeat it. The comment on ticket 901 also timed out but had saved. I retried it with its idempotency key and confirmed there is exactly one comment.
- **Other releases:** `session-svc` `r-175` was created exactly at `2026-09-24T00:00Z`, so it is outside the period. `billing-api` `r-154` was created by a rollback, so it isn't audited.
